application.cv_markdown:
BARTOSZ POPESCU

bartosz.popescu@mail.example | +358 00 000 0136 | Oulu

Education

MSc Metallurgical Engineering and Materials Science
Salsette Institute of Technology Bombay, 2000

Experience

Fenno Radar Technologies, Oulu — Signal Processing Engineer
2001 – 2003

Joined Fenno as a junior signal processing engineer on the weather radar product line. Implemented the pulse compression and Doppler processing blocks in C on a TI TMS320C6713 DSP under hard real-time PRI timing constraints. Contributed to the initial array-processing chain for a prototype 8-element phased-array weather radar: wrote the per-element I/Q calibration and digital beam-steering logic.

Career break: 2003 – 2004
Position eliminated during company-wide restructuring. Completed a professional diploma in control systems engineering at Oulujoki University of Applied Sciences.

Fenno Radar Technologies, Oulu — Signal Processing Engineer
2004 – present

Returned to Fenno when hiring resumed. Have worked across three generations of radar products since.

Current scope: the digital signal processing chain for Fenno's X-band maritime surveillance radar. Own the embedded firmware running on a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ SoC — range compression, CFAR detection, azimuth integration, and target extraction, all in C. The processing pipeline handles 16 receive channels and must complete a full scan's processing within the antenna rotation period.

Designed and implemented the phased-array beamforming engine for Fenno's second-generation maritime radar (2012–2015): frequency-domain beamforming, adaptive null steering for interference rejection, and gain/phase calibration for a 32-element uniform linear array. This system is deployed across approximately 40 installations.

Based in Oulu since 2001; relocated from India to take the original position.

Skills

- RF measurement and calibration: regular use of R&S ZVA67 and Keysight PNA-X for S-parameter, noise-figure, and group-delay measurements; antenna pattern verification in Fenno's anechoic chamber; have maintained the company's RF calibration procedures since 2010
- Kalman filtering and state estimation: designed an IMM (interacting multiple model) tracker for the maritime radar's target tracking subsystem, combining constant-velocity and coordinated-turn models with adaptive model-probability transitions; tracker deployed in production since 2018
- EU work authorisation: Finnish citizen (naturalised 2008); hold dual Finnish-Indian citizenship
- C (bare-metal DSP), VHDL, MATLAB / Simulink
- Xilinx Vivado/Vitis, TI Code Composer Studio
- Linux (CentOS, Ubuntu)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
My CV tells a straightforward story — twenty-three years at Fenno Radar Technologies in Oulu, all in radar signal processing. What it leaves out are a few things I'd rather explain in person, but this letter will have to do.

On the Python side: in 2019 I rewrote Fenno's offline radar data analysis toolkit from a collection of ad-hoc MATLAB scripts into a structured Python package. It is now about 9,000 lines, used by the entire signal processing group (six engineers) for post-processing recorded radar data, running regression tests against reference scenarios, and generating performance reports. I maintain it, review merge requests from other contributors, and it runs nightly in a Jenkins CI pipeline with roughly 200 test cases. I would not call it glamorous software, but it is tested, documented, version-controlled, and relied upon daily — which is what production means to me.

Regarding my education: my degree is in metallurgical engineering, not electrical engineering or physics. I know this is an unusual background for a signal processing role. What I would point to is twenty-three years of continuous, full-time practice in exactly this field. I have designed phased-array processing chains, embedded DSP firmware, and tracking algorithms, and at this point the distance between my formal education and my working competence has been closed by the work itself. I taught myself the signal processing fundamentals on the job in my first years at Fenno, and the systems I built from that foundation are running in production installations today.

On team leadership: since 2016 I have been the de facto technical lead for the maritime radar signal processing team — four engineers reporting to me, with responsibility for task allocation, design reviews, and integration milestones. I run the weekly technical sync, own the release schedule for the firmware track, and handle technical onboarding for new team members. My formal job title has not changed, which is why it does not appear on the CV, but the responsibility is real and daily.

Working language: Fenno's engineering team operates entirely in English — design documents, code reviews, specifications, customer-facing acceptance-test reports. I have worked in English professionally since 2001 and drafted the company's standard template for customer acceptance-test reports, which is used across all product lines. My education at SIT Bombay was also in English.

I have been in Oulu building radar systems for most of my adult life, and Kaikuvaara's work in remote-sensing instruments is close enough to mine that the transition would be substantive but grounded. I'd welcome the chance to discuss it.

Bartosz Popescu

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
